Web.Page.Me.Lore.Description: What Hoshi knows about you — how she should address you, your languages and interests.
Web.Audience.Guild.Label: Guild
Web.Audience.Guild.Description: Guild-wide features that apply to the whole Discord, regardless of audience.
Web.Audience.Alliance.Label: Alliance
Web.Audience.Alliance.Description: This guild is a single alliance's own Discord.
Web.Audience.Server.Label: Server
Web.Audience.Server.Description: This guild serves a whole STFC server.
Web.Audience.VeilGroup.Label: Veil Group
Web.Audience.VeilGroup.Description: This guild serves a veil group (a coalition of servers).
Web.Audience.Community.Label: Community
Web.Audience.Community.Description: A general Discord not tied to one alliance or server.
Web.Feature.Absences.Title: Absences
Web.Feature.Absences.Description: Members can report an upcoming absence; a kept-updated report of who's away posts to a public channel (and a staff-only copy) so leadership doesn't need to ask around.
Web.Feature.AllianceTagRoles.Title: Alliance Tag Roles
Web.Feature.AllianceTagRoles.Description: Gives every member with a linked player a role named after their alliance's tag, so you can see at a glance who is from where. Roles are made for your own server(s) only; members from elsewhere share a single foreign-alliance role. Roles can be created automatically, and the tag can be rewritten to plain letters, lowercased, or wrapped in a prefix/suffix.
Web.Feature.ServerTagRoles.Title: Server Tag Roles
Web.Feature.ServerTagRoles.Description: Gives every member with a linked player a role named after the server they play on, so a coalition or veil-group Discord shows at a glance who is from where. You pick or create one role per server this Discord is set up for; everyone from anywhere else shares a single foreign-server role.
Web.Feature.ConditionalRoles.Title: Conditional Roles
Web.Feature.ConditionalRoles.Description: Grants a role while a rule you write matches a member's other roles, and takes it away again when it stops matching. Rules combine roles with and / or / not and can nest freely, and a condition you build once — say the list of your alliance tags — can be reused across rules.
Web.Feature.AiBackend.Title: AI Provider
Web.Feature.AiBackend.Description: The shared AI backend for this whole Discord: which language-model provider to use (Google Gemini or a local Ollama model), the API key, and the model choices. Every AI-powered feature — AI Chat, Member Lore, Announcement Forwarder — runs on this one configuration, so there's a single AI account per guild.
Web.Feature.AiChat.Title: AI Chat
Web.Feature.AiChat.Description: Lets the bot answer questions conversationally (via Google Gemini) in a configurable set of listen channels, grounded in a configurable set of knowledge channels. It can also build a genuine memory over time — notable community events, past conversations, and its own history with individual members — so answers feel like they come from someone who was actually there. Each guild uses its own Gemini API key.
Web.Feature.AlertsOptIn.Title: Alerts Opt-In
Web.Feature.AlertsOptIn.Description: Lets members opt in/out of a role that receives raid/shield alert pings, instead of everyone getting pinged by default.
Web.Feature.AllianceTournament.Title: Alliance Tournament Announcements
Web.Feature.AllianceTournament.Descripti: Advance-warning announcement when a new Alliance Tournament event is scheduled.
Web.Feature.AnnouncementForwarder.Title: Announcement Forwarder
Web.Feature.AnnouncementForwarder.Descri: Auto-translates official announcements (e.g. Scopely's English STFC news) posted in the source channels and reposts them as a branded translation in a destination channel, so members who don't read the source language still see them.
Web.Feature.Announcements.Title: Announcements
Web.Feature.Announcements.Description: Staff-published announcements with read tracking and unread reminders — usable by any audience, not alliance-specific.
Web.Feature.AnonymousMessaging.Title: Anonymous Messages
Web.Feature.AnonymousMessaging.Descripti: Members can send a message to leadership without revealing who sent it — usable by any audience.
Web.Feature.ClientRelease.Title: Client Release Announcements
Web.Feature.ClientRelease.Description: Announces when a new STFC game client version is released (Windows, macOS, Android, iOS) — relevant to any guild, not just alliances.
Web.Feature.CommandBridge.Title: Command Bridge
Web.Feature.CommandBridge.Description: The per-alliance "Kommandobrücke" hub messages (User/Staff/Friends) — the member- and staff-facing entry point most other features' buttons live on. Pick a channel per bridge and publish it; buttons appear as their features are enabled for this alliance.
Web.Feature.Diplomacy.Title: Diplomacy
Web.Feature.Diplomacy.Description: Tracks and announces this alliance's diplomatic status toward other alliances via /set-diplomacy.
Web.Feature.HoshiSay.Title: Hoshi Say
Web.Feature.HoshiSay.Description: Lets an admin have Hoshi compose a message in her own voice (via the AI backend) and post it as a plain chat line into the current channel — e.g. to comfort or address a member. The /hoshi-say command is limited to members holding the configured allowed role, which is the permission gate.
Web.Feature.InfiniteIncursions.Title: Infinite Incursions Announcements
Web.Feature.InfiniteIncursions.Descripti: Advance-warning announcement when a new Infinite Incursions event is scheduled.
Web.Feature.MemberLore.Title: Member Lore
Web.Feature.MemberLore.Description: The bot DM-interviews members (optional, opt-out) to learn who they are — how to address them, what they're into, funny stories about each other — so it can chat like a real member of the community.
Web.Feature.MemberOnboarding.Title: Member Onboarding
Web.Feature.MemberOnboarding.Description: Opt-in: DMs members that Player Assignment couldn't place automatically, asking them to confirm the bot's best guess or type their in-game player. Off by default — leave it off to resolve missing assignments only via Player Assignment's admin table, without ever DMing members.
Web.Feature.NicknameSync.Title: Nickname Sync
Web.Feature.NicknameSync.Description: Renames members' Discord nicknames to match their linked in-game player, optionally prefixing a server and/or alliance tag (e.g. [EU164][XYZ] Name) to disambiguate foreign players.
Web.Feature.OpsLevelRoles.Title: Ops Level Roles
Web.Feature.OpsLevelRoles.Description: Assigns each member one of seven Discord roles matching their current STFC Ops Level tier (G1-G7), kept in sync from imported player data — one set of roles for the whole guild.
Web.Feature.PlayerLink.Title: Player Assignment
Web.Feature.PlayerLink.Description: Links members to their STFC player by matching Discord nicknames against the whole player catalog — which drives rank/ops/nickname role sync. Confident matches link automatically; everyone else you assign by hand on the member page. Never messages members.
Web.Feature.RaidAlerts.Title: Raid Alerts
Web.Feature.RaidAlerts.Description: Members can report an incoming raid via /raid, posting a public alert to whichever channel(s) are configured below.
Web.Feature.RankRoles.Title: Rank Roles
Web.Feature.RankRoles.Description: Assigns each member one of five Discord roles matching their current STFC in-alliance rank (Admiral/Commodore/Premier/Operative/Agent), kept in sync from imported player data — one set of roles for the whole guild.
Web.Feature.BotSupport.Title: Bot Support
Web.Feature.BotSupport.Description: Adds a Help button to the user Command Bridge that points members at the channel where they can ask about the bot itself.
Web.Feature.ChannelGuide.Title: Channel Guide
Web.Feature.ChannelGuide.Description: Adds a "Help with something else" button to the user Command Bridge showing a message you write, pointing members at the channels where their question belongs.
Web.Editor.BotSupport.Intro: With this on, the user Command Bridge carries a Help button. Clicking it shows a short note naming the channel below, so a member with a bot problem knows where to raise it. The bot only mentions that channel — it never posts there, so it needs no permissions on it.
Web.Editor.BotSupport.Channel.Usage: Where members are sent for help with the bot itself. Mentioned only — the bot never posts here.
Web.Editor.ChannelGuide.Intro: With this on, the user Command Bridge carries a Help with something else button showing the message below — the place to send members whose question isn't one the other buttons cover. Use the pickers underneath to add a channel or a role: Discord only makes those clickable in their <#id> / <@&id> form, and text copied out of Discord only looks like one. Anything recognisable you type or paste is converted when you save. {commander} is replaced with the member's name.
Web.Editor.ChannelGuide.Message.Label: Shown when a member clicks "Help with something else". Markdown works, and {commander} becomes their name.
Web.Guild.DependencyNote.BotSupport.Comm: The Help button rides on the user Command Bridge.
Web.Guild.DependencyNote.ChannelGuide.Co: The button rides on the user Command Bridge.
Web.Feature.ReadReceipts.Title: Read Confirmation
Web.Feature.ReadReceipts.Description: Adds a ✅ confirm button to the kinds of post you choose, and collects what a member still hasn't read into one list they can open from the Command Bridge.
Web.Editor.ReadReceipts.Intro: Pick which kinds of post ask members to confirm they've read them. Each post records the answer when it is posted, so changing this only affects new ones — a post already carrying a button keeps counting, and switching a kind on never retroactively asks about posts nobody was shown a button for.
Web.Feature.RoeViolationReports.Title: RoE Violation Reports
Web.Feature.RoeViolationReports.Descript: Members can report a suspected Rules of Engagement violation for staff to review.
Web.Feature.ServerStatus.Title: Server Status
Web.Feature.ServerStatus.Description: Announces when a tracked STFC server goes up/down or in/out of maintenance — relevant to any guild tracking a server, not just alliances.
Web.Feature.ServicesRoleSync.Title: Services Role Sync
Web.Feature.ServicesRoleSync.Description: Keeps the Territory Capture Services role in lock-step with the rank roles that can activate services (Admiral/Commodore): every alliance member holding either rank role gets the Services role, and anyone who no longer qualifies loses it. Needs Rank Roles and Territory Capture Service Reminders configured.
Web.Feature.ShieldReminders.Title: Shield Reminders
Web.Feature.ShieldReminders.Description: Members can set a reminder for when their shield expires; the bot pings them as it nears expiration and posts a public alert if it actually expires unrenewed.
Web.Feature.StfcNews.Title: STFC News
Web.Feature.StfcNews.Description: Pings this guild's Admin channel when a new Alliance Tournament or Infinite Incursions post appears on the official STFC blog, and lets admins confirm the event date so it feeds the relevant notify feature.
Web.Feature.TerritoryCapture.Title: Territory Capture Reminders
Web.Feature.TerritoryCapture.Description: Zone-slot and rank role sync, plus the weekly/daily Territory Capture digest summarizing owned zones and next capture times.
Web.Feature.TerritoryCaptureSignOff.Desc: Lets members sign off from an upcoming territory capture: the capture digests and reminders ask them to, and carry a button per zone. Each click records an absence for that capture window. Nothing to configure — needs Territory Capture and Absences enabled.
Web.Feature.TerritoryCaptureServiceRemin: After each capture ends, reminds the officers who can activate services which ones to turn on for that zone, in its own channel. Curate the per-zone service list on its Service Selection page; a zone with no selection lists all of its services.
Web.Feature.Tickets.Title: Tickets
Web.Feature.Tickets.Description: Members can open a private support thread with staff via the hub button — usable by any audience.
Web.Editor.Absences.ReportChannel.Usage: Where the public, kept-updated absence report is posted. Each entry respects the member's chosen privacy setting.
Web.Editor.Absences.ReportStaffChannel.U: A staff-only copy of the report that always shows every absence in full, ignoring members' privacy settings.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.Intro: The guild-wide AI backend. These settings — provider, API key, and model choices — are shared by every AI-powered feature (AI Chat, Member Lore, Announcement Forwarder). One AI account per guild.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.Provider.Label: Which language model this guild uses. Gemini (Google Cloud, needs its own API key) or Ollama (local model on the shared server, no key needed).
Web.Editor.AiBackend.ApiKey.Label: This guild's own Google Gemini API key. Used for all AI answers and stored encrypted at rest.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.KeySaved: A key is saved. Enter a new value to replace it.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.ModelLabelOllama: Ollama model. Leave empty for the server's default model.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.ModelLabelGemini: Gemini model. Leave empty for the default ({model}).
Web.Editor.AiBackend.RouterOffOption: Off — always use the main model
Web.Editor.AiBackend.ImageEmbeddingProvi: Not in use yet — Hoshi does not index images, so this has no effect today. It is here so the choice is recorded before image indexing lands. Kept separate from text embeddings on purpose: a guild can keep cheap local text embeddings and still pay for the handful of images worth searching.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.EmbeddingProvider.L: Which backend powers semantic search (paraphrase-aware knowledge lookup) and memory recall. Independent of the AI provider above — you can chat with Gemini while keeping Ollama embeddings, or vice versa.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.EmbeddingProvider.U: Gemini Embedding options reuse this guild's Gemini API key (set above) — no separate key needed, but a Gemini choice stays disabled until a key is configured. Switching doesn't need a manual re-index: existing content re-embeds automatically over the next few scheduled passes (a brief window where search quietly skips not-yet-re-embedded content is expected and self-corrects). Gemini Embedding 1 is text-only; Gemini Embedding 2 additionally supports image/video/audio/PDF input at the API level, though Hoshi doesn't index those yet.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.GateModel.Label: A small, fast model that pre-screens messages in listen channels: it decides whether a message the bot wasn't directly asked is even worth a full answer, so the bot doesn't run (and show "typing…" for) an expensive answer on every bit of chatter. It only ever stays quiet on clear non-questions — anything unsure still gets a full answer. Direct @mentions always answer and skip this.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.GateUsageOllama: Leave empty to use the server's default (the Ollama__GateModel deployment setting — the gate is off only if that's unset too). Enter a pulled model to override it for this guild, or off to disable the gate here.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.GateUsageGemini: Leave empty for the default ({model}). Enter a model to override it, or off to disable the gate.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.RouterModel.Label: A small/cheap model that answers simple questions and classifies each question's complexity; complex questions escalate to the main Model above. Leave empty to always use the main Model.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.RouterTip: Free-tier tip: set {model} here — it allows far more requests per day than the main flash model, so the small quota is only spent on genuinely complex questions.
Web.Editor.AiBackend.RouterOffOllamaPlac: Off — a smaller pulled model to enable
Web.Editor.AiBackend.RouterModel.Usage: Leave empty (or off) to always use the main Model. Enter a model to enable complexity routing.
Web.Editor.AiChat.Intro1: The bot listens to every message in the listen channels and answers when it has a genuinely helpful reply (staying silent otherwise). It always answers when addressed by its nickname or @mention. Answers are grounded in the recent conversation plus the configured knowledge channels. The language-model provider, API key and models are shared across every AI feature and configured on the AI Provider page.
Web.Editor.AiChat.Intro2: Knowledge channels (also forums, or whole categories) are the sources the bot draws on to ground its answers — a forum contributes all of its posts. Their priority controls which sources the answer search prefers — Preferred is boosted, Last resort is only used when the higher tiers have no answer. A channel belongs to exactly one tier (adding it to one removes it from the others).
Web.Editor.AiChat.ListenUsage: Channels the bot reads and answers in.
Web.Editor.AiChat.KnowledgePreferredUsag: Curated/internal channels. Hits here are boosted in the answer search.
Web.Editor.AiChat.KnowledgeLastResortUsa: E.g. external content (content creators / Scopely). Used only when the preferred/normal sources have no answer.
Web.Editor.AiChat.SystemPrompt.Label: Extra personality/behaviour instruction, prepended to the default prompt.
Web.Editor.AiChat.StreamResponses.Label: Stream answers live
Web.Editor.AiChat.StreamResponses.Usage: Post an answer as a placeholder / typing indicator and edit it in place as the model writes, instead of one message at the end. Nice for slow local (Ollama) models; off by default.
Web.Editor.AiChat.MemoryEnabled.Label: Let Hoshi remember events
Web.Editor.AiChat.MemoryEnabled.Usage: Hoshi distils notable community events from chat into memories she recalls later in conversation. Needs embeddings configured (see the AI Provider page). Review, edit, or forget them here.
Web.Editor.AiChat.SearchLanguage.Label: Language for the full-text search over the knowledge sources (controls word-stemming). Prefilled from the server language.
Web.Editor.AlertsOptIn.Role.Usage: Role members opt into via the hub's 'manage alerts' button, to receive raid/shield pings.
Web.Editor.AllianceTournament.Intro: Advance-warning announcement when a new Alliance Tournament event is scheduled. Not scoped to a specific server — every guild tracking any server (see Scope) is notified, since Alliance Tournament isn't currently known to be server/region-specific. Currently fed by a one-time seed, not a live sync — see StfcEventStatus for why.
Web.Editor.AnnouncementForwarder.Sources: Channels to watch for official announcements (e.g. the crossposted Scopely news channel).
Web.Editor.AnnouncementForwarder.Channel: Where the translated announcement is posted.
Web.Editor.AnnouncementForwarder.TargetL: Language to translate into. Leave empty to use the server's Discord language.
Web.Editor.AnnouncementForwarder.CatchUp: How far back (in hours) to look for a missed announcement — e.g. one posted while the bot was down. Only messages newer than this are ever caught up, so a long-idle source channel doesn't get its whole history dumped into the destination. Leave empty for the default ({hours} hours).
Web.Editor.Announcements.TestChannel.Usa: A dry-run destination. With one picked, the publish prompt offers it beside the real channel, so staff can see a finished announcement in place before the guild does. It's a real publish — same embed, same read-receipt button — just somewhere harmless.
Web.Editor.Announcements.DraftChannel.Us: Where staff post announcement drafts (plain message, attachments allowed) before publishing them.
Web.Editor.Announcements.WarningsRole.Us: Pinged when a High-severity announcement is published.
Web.Editor.AnonymousMessaging.Channel.Us: Where anonymous messages submitted via the hub button are posted.
Web.Editor.ClientRelease.Intro: Announces when a new STFC game client version is released for Windows, macOS, Android, or iOS. Linux has no known version-check source yet. Each announcement posts to the channels below and pings only that platform's role — members opt in/out of a platform's role via the hub's "manage alerts" button.
Web.Editor.ClientRelease.ChannelsUsage: Every configured platform release is posted to each of these channels.
Web.Editor.ClientRelease.PlatformRolesUs: The role pinged when each platform releases a new version — one per platform, shared across all audiences. Members opt in/out via the alerts hub button.
Web.Editor.CommandBridge.Intro: Each Command Bridge is a persistent hub message with action buttons, scoped to this alliance. Pick a channel per bridge and click Publish to (re)post it — the bot posts it shortly after. Which buttons appear is controlled by enabling/disabling the underlying features (for this alliance) on this Features page. While the Command Bridge is disabled its hubs are not (re)posted.
Web.Editor.CommandBridge.StaffBridgeSubt: "Kommandobrücke Führungsstab" — post this to a staff-only channel.
Web.Editor.CommandBridge.FriendsBridgeSu: "Kommandobrücke Freunde" — a trimmed hub for allied/friend guilds.
Web.Editor.CommandBridge.ChannelUsage: Where this Command Bridge hub message is posted.
Web.Editor.CommandBridge.StatusStillQueu: Still queued — is the bot running?
Web.Editor.CommandBridge.StatusFailed: {icon:Error} Discord rejected it: {error}. Check the bot's permissions on that channel, then publish again.
Web.Editor.CommandBridge.NoButtons: No buttons are assigned to this bridge.
Web.Editor.Diplomacy.Channel.Usage: Where diplomacy status changes (/set-diplomacy) are announced.
Web.Editor.Diplomacy.DiplomatRole.Usage: Role for members who can run /set-diplomacy for this guild's alliance.
Web.Editor.HoshiSay.AllowedRole.Usage: Members with this role may run /hoshi-say. The command posts into whatever channel it's used in, so an admin just stands in the target channel and runs it — role membership is the permission gate.
Web.Editor.InfiniteIncursions.Intro: Advance-warning announcement when a new Infinite Incursions event is scheduled. Not scoped to a specific server — every guild tracking any server (see Scope) is notified, since Infinite Incursions aren't currently known to be server/region-specific. Currently fed by a one-time seed, not a live sync — see StfcEventStatus for why.
Web.Editor.MemberLore.MemberRole.Usage: Only members holding this role are interviewed. Leave empty to fall back to the alliance's configured member role.
Web.Editor.MemberLore.CompletedRole.Usag: Granted to a member once they finish their interview, e.g. an introduced/known role. Leave empty for none.
Web.Editor.MemberLore.MaxInterviewsPerDa: How many interview DMs the bot sends per day. Paces the campaign and stays clear of Discord's DM rate limits. Empty → a conservative default (10).
Web.Editor.MemberLore.CampaignUsage: Turn this on to start the campaign. The bot then DMs eligible members (most chat-active first, up to the daily cap). New members become eligible automatically.
Web.Editor.MemberLore.ProgressLine: Invited {invited} · in progress {inProgress} · completed {completed} · declined {declined} · undeliverable {undeliverable}
Web.Editor.MemberLore.NotesUsage: Interview transcripts are turned into per-member notes that Hoshi uses in chat. Review the crowdsourced stories about others and edit any member's notes here.
Web.Editor.MemberLoreInterviewsAdmin.Int: Every member the bot has invited to (or is running) a DM interview, and where they are in it. Bot-managed — status/progress come from the interview job/DM conversation, not editable here.
Web.Editor.MemberLoreInterviewsAdmin.Emp: No interviews yet — enable the campaign to start inviting members.
Web.Editor.MemberNotesAdmin.Heading: Member Lore — Notes & Review
Web.Editor.MemberNotesAdmin.Intro: Community notes extracted from interviews. Members' own answers are applied directly; stories about others land here for approval before Hoshi uses them.
Web.Editor.MemberOnboarding.HowItWorksUs: When active, the bot DMs members that Player Assignment couldn't place automatically, asking them to confirm the bot's best guess or type their in-game name. It only sends buttons and a short form — never free-text chat. Once a member confirms, they're linked and their roles sync automatically. Requires Player Assignment to be enabled and configured.
Web.Editor.MemberOnboarding.MaxInvitesPe: How many onboarding DMs the bot sends per day. Paces the outreach and stays clear of Discord's DM rate limits. Empty → a conservative default (10).
Web.Editor.MemberOnboarding.CampaignUsag: Turn this on to start DMing unresolved members (up to the daily cap). Off → the bot links only confident matches silently and leaves the rest for the admin table.
Web.Editor.MemberOnboarding.ProgressLine: Unresolved {unresolved} · DM sent {dmSent} · matched {resolved} · declined {declined} · undeliverable {undeliverable}
Web.Editor.NicknameSync.HowItWorksUsage: Each member's nickname is set to their main linked player's in-game name. Add server/alliance tags below to tell foreign players apart. Members with no linked player are left alone, as are members holding an excluded role. The bot can only rename members whose highest role is below its own.
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.HowItWorksUs: Each member with a linked player gets one role, named after the alliance that player is in. Per-alliance roles are only made for your own server(s) — the servers of your linked alliances, plus any server this Discord tracks in its own right; everyone from elsewhere shares the foreign-alliance role below. Changing alliance swaps the role; members with no linked player are never touched. The options below only decide how a new role is named: matching an existing role is always case-insensitive and accepts both the original and the plain-letter spelling, so changing an option never leaves your existing roles behind.
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.CreateMissin: Create roles that don't exist yet
Off: only alliances that already have a matching role get one assigned, so you decide which roles exist by creating them yourself.
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.LatinizeLabe: Rewrite the tag in plain letters
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.LatinizeUsag: Uses the letter each character looks like: ĶÅØŞ becomes KAOS, ВСТК becomes BCTK. Characters with no look-alike (Japanese, Korean, Chinese) are left as they are.
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.LowercaseLab: Name new roles in lower case
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.LowercaseUsa: Affects the name of newly created roles only — who gets which role never depends on upper or lower case.
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.AffixUsage: Optional text placed around the tag. Handy to keep tag roles apart from your other roles, especially with short tags.
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.BoundRolesUs: The roles this feature currently manages — one per alliance it has seen. These are the roles it will take off a member who changes alliance.
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.NoBoundRoles: None yet — they appear after the next sync (within 10 minutes).
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.NoAllianceRo: Given to a member whose linked player currently has no alliance. Leave blank to give them no role at all.
Web.Editor.AllianceTagRoles.ForeignAllia: One shared role for members whose alliance is on a server this Discord doesn't track. They get this instead of their own tag role, so a Discord with visitors from all over doesn't collect a role per foreign alliance. Leave blank to give them no role at all.
Web.Editor.ServerTagRoles.HowItWorksUsag: Each member with a linked player gets one role, named after the server that player is on. The list below is your own servers — the servers of your linked alliances, plus any server this Discord tracks in its own right; everyone from elsewhere shares the foreign-server role. Moving server swaps the role; members with no linked player are never touched. Nothing is created until you pick or create a role yourself, so a server you leave blank simply gets none.
Web.Editor.ServerTagRoles.ServersUsage: One row per server this Discord is set up for. Pick an existing role or let it be created for you, named after the server number.
Web.Editor.ServerTagRoles.NoServers: No servers yet — link an alliance or a server under Audience first.
Web.Editor.ServerTagRoles.ForeignServerR: One shared role for members playing on a server this Discord isn't set up for. They get this instead of a server role of their own. Leave blank to give them no role at all.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.HowItWorksUs: A rule grants one role while its condition matches, and removes it again as soon as it doesn't — so the role always reflects the rule. Conditions are built from has role checks combined with all of, any of and not, nested as deeply as you like. Only roles a rule targets are ever touched; everything else a member holds is left alone. A rule that isn't finished grants nothing at all rather than guessing.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.RulesCardUsa: Each rule names a role to grant and the condition that decides who gets it.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.ConditionsCa: Build a condition once and reference it from any rule — with «and» in one, with «and not» in another.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.RulesIntro: A member holds the target role exactly while the condition below it matches. Changes take effect on the next sync, within about ten minutes.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.ConditionsIn: Named conditions have no role of their own — they exist to be referenced from rules and from other conditions.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.NoRulesYet: No rules yet. Add one below.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.NoConditions: No conditions yet. Add one below.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.CopyIsInacti: The copy is created inactive, so it grants nothing until you have checked it over.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.IncompleteWa: This rule is unfinished, so it currently grants nothing. Pick a role to grant and complete every part of the condition.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.ConditionInc: This condition is unfinished, so every rule using it currently grants nothing.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.CycleRejecte: «{name}» would end up referring back to itself, so it can't be saved. Remove the reference that leads back to it.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.ConditionInU: «{name}» is still used by: {usages}. Remove those references first.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.DuplicateNam: A condition called «{name}» already exists. Pick a different name.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.KindInHomeAl: is in one of our alliances
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.KindOnHomeSe: plays on one of our servers
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.SearchPlaceh: type at least 2 letters to search…
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.PlayerFactsH: The last two need a linked player. For a member without one the answer is unknown, so the rule leaves them exactly as they are — pair it with «has a linked player» if you want a decision either way.
Web.Editor.ConditionalRoles.NotTakesOneH: «not» inverts exactly one thing — use a group inside it to negate several.
Web.Editor.RankRoles.NoRankRole.Usage: Given to a member whose linked player currently has no rank — which, since a rank only exists inside an alliance, means anyone who has left theirs. Leave blank to give them no role at all.
Web.Editor.NicknameSync.ExcludedRoles.Us: Members holding any of these roles are never renamed.
Web.Editor.NicknameSync.MemberSuffixUsag: Members can set a short alias on their own profile page, which is appended in parentheses: [TAG] Player (Suffix). It's dropped automatically when the nickname would exceed Discord's 32-character limit. Turn this off to keep member-authored text out of this server's nicknames — their suffix stays set for other communities.
Web.Editor.PlayerLink.HowItWorksUsage: The bot matches each member's Discord nickname against the whole player catalog and links confident matches automatically — a globally-unique name, or a unique match within one of your alliances — with no message to the member. Everyone else (members from other alliances/servers, renamed players, alts) you assign by hand on the member page.
Web.Editor.PlayerLink.StatusUsage.one: {count} member couldn't be matched automatically and is waiting for manual assignment. To adjust roles yourself, see the Rank Roles and Ops-Level Roles features.
Web.Editor.PlayerLink.StatusUsage.other: {count} members couldn't be matched automatically and are waiting for manual assignment. To adjust roles yourself, see the Rank Roles and Ops-Level Roles features.
Web.Editor.PlayerLink.UnlinkedRole.Usage: Given to every member who has no in-game player linked yet, and taken away again the moment one is. Useful as a nudge, or to gate channels until someone is identified. Leave blank to assign nothing. Bots are ignored.
Web.Editor.PlayerAssignmentsAdmin.Intro: Assign each member to their in-game player(s). The links are global to the person — they apply in every server they share with Hoshi. The {icon:Text.Primary} marks the player that represents them here, which is what drives this server's automatic role assignment (rank, ops level, nickname); members can also set it themselves on their own profile page. A player can be linked to multiple Discord accounts (e.g. alt accounts).

Web.Editor.RoeViolationReports.Channel.U: Where /report-roe-violation reports are posted — must be a Forum channel.
Web.Editor.RoeViolationReports.DiplomatR: Per-alliance role pinged in the report thread once the reporter marks a case ready. This is the same Diplomat role as the Diplomacy feature.
Web.Editor.ServerStatus.Intro: Announces when a tracked STFC server (see this guild's Scope) goes up/down or in/out of maintenance. Currently fed by a one-time seed, not a live sync — see StfcServerStatus for why.
Web.Editor.ServicesRoleSync.Intro: When enabled, this alliance's Territory Capture Services role is kept in sync with the rank roles that can activate services (Admiral and Commodore): every alliance member holding either rank role is given the Services role, and anyone who no longer qualifies has it removed. Configure the source rank roles on the Rank Roles feature. The two roles below are shared with the Territory Capture Service Reminders and Alliance Settings pages — editing them here updates them there too.
Web.Editor.ServicesRoleSync.ServicesRole: The role assigned to Admiral/Commodore alliance members. Shared with the Territory Capture Service Reminders editor. Leave blank to create a dedicated role.
Web.Editor.ServicesRoleSync.MemberRole.U: This alliance's general membership role — only its holders receive the Services role. Shared with Alliance Settings.
Web.Editor.TerritoryCaptureSignOff.Intro: When enabled, this alliance's Territory Capture digests and capture reminders ask members to sign off if they can't make a capture, and carry a "Sign off for …" button per zone. A click records an absence for that capture window, which the member can then see and manage like any other. There is nothing to configure here — turn it off and the digests simply drop the request and the buttons.
Web.Editor.TerritoryCaptureServiceRemind: About five minutes after each of this alliance's captures ends, Hoshi posts an "activate services" reminder for the officers who hold the in-game permission — into its own channel, separate from the capture digests. Curate which services it names per zone under Service Selection; a zone with no selection lists all of its services.
Where the post-capture 'activate services' reminder for officers is posted.
The officer role pinged by the post-capture "activate services" reminder. Leave blank to create a dedicated role.
Curate each owned zone's services into must-have / nice-to-have for the "activate services" reminder. Unconfigured zones list all their services.
Web.Editor.StfcNews.Intro: Watches the official STFC blog (startrekfleetcommand.com) for new posts whose title mentions "Alliance Tournament" or "Infinite Incursions", and pings this guild's Admin channel (see Global Settings) with the post's title and link, plus a button to enter the event date once an admin has read the post. Pairing/schedule details inside the post are not parsed out automatically.
Web.Editor.TerritoryCapture.DigestChanne: Where this alliance's weekly/daily capture digests are posted.
Web.Editor.TerritoryCapture.ZoneSlotRole: One role per owned-zone-slot the alliance currently holds this week (the "Zone Slots: N/5" cap shown in-game) — not days of the week. Slot N's role goes to every member with an owned zone in that slot.
Web.Editor.TerritoryCapture.WeeklyMentio: The role pinged on the weekly digest (the daily digest pings the specific zone-slot roles for tomorrow instead). This is the alliance's absence-clean notification role — the same setting as on the Absences page; editing it here updates it there too.
Web.Editor.TerritoryCapture.DigestSchedu: When the weekly and daily digests post, as local times in this alliance's timezone ({timezone}, DST-aware — change it on Alliance Settings). Weekly posts the day before the capture week (Thursday); daily posts every day. 30-minute steps.
Web.Editor.TerritoryCapture.Instructions: Free-text "Instructions from {Command Staff}" section shown on the weekly/daily digest (e.g. attendance/armada expectations).
Web.Editor.ServiceSelectionAdmin.Intro: Curate which of a zone's services the Territory Capture "activate services" reminder tells officers to activate, split into two priorities — must have (mandatory services) and nice to have (optional services, on request). A zone with no selection lists all its services instead. Only zones the alliance currently owns are shown; available services come from the territory.lol sync.
Web.Editor.ServiceSelectionAdmin.NoZones: This alliance owns no zones yet — nothing to configure.
Web.Editor.ServiceSelectionAdmin.NoServi: No services synced for this zone on the alliance's server. Run the sync on Territory Services first.
Web.Editor.ServiceSelectionAdmin.MustHav: Mandatory services — listed first, in game order.
Web.Editor.ServiceSelectionAdmin.MutualE: A service picked as must-have is automatically removed from nice-to-have, and vice versa.

Web.Editor.AiChatMemoryAdmin.Heading: Hoshi's Memories
Web.Editor.AiChatMemoryAdmin.Intro: What Hoshi remembers about the community — formed automatically from chat. Edit the wording, re-weight importance (salience 1–5, higher = recalled more readily and resists fading), or forget any memory. Low-salience, long-unused ones fade on their own over time.

Web.Editor.AiChatHealth.NoCallsRecorded: No calls recorded yet — the bot writes a row the first time it runs a chat or embedding call for this guild.

Web.Wizard.StepHeader: Step {step} of {total} — {title}. Every step is optional; you can always adjust things later via Scope/Settings, or per-feature via Features.
Web.Wizard.WelcomeLead1: This wizard walks you through the essentials for a new guild: which audience it serves, linking your alliance(s)/server(s), a few core channels/roles, and making sure someone besides the server owner can manage the bot.
Web.Wizard.WelcomeLead2: Nothing here is mandatory — skip anything and configure it later. Turning individual features on/off now happens from Features, not this wizard.

Web.Wizard.CoreLead: A curated subset most guilds need right away — the full list is on the
Web.Wizard.CoreLeaveBlank: Leave any field below empty to have Hoshi Bot create it for you.
Web.Wizard.Creating: Creating anything left blank on Discord...
Web.Wizard.CategoryLabel: Channel group for anything created below
Web.Wizard.AdminAccessLead: Members holding any of these roles can manage this guild's Hoshi Bot settings even without Discord's "Manage Server" permission — so setup doesn't leave the server owner as the only possible admin.
Web.Wizard.ReviewLead: Anything left unset here just stays editable later via Scope/Settings — finishing doesn't require completing every step. Turning individual features on/off, and their own channel/role settings, happens from Features.
Web.Wizard.CreateError: Could not create a channel/role on Discord — does the bot have Manage Channels/Manage Roles permission in this server?
Web.Audit.Heading: Channel Permission Check
Web.Audit.Lead: Define the exact permission overwrite a role should have on a channel, then audit live Discord permissions against it.
Web.Audit.ManageRolesNo: No — Fix actions will fail entirely
Web.Audit.RoleTip: Tip: for Hoshi Bot to reliably manage every role's channel permissions, place its role directly below your top admin/owner role in Server Settings → Roles. Any role positioned above the bot's role can't be fixed here — Discord requires a bot's own role to outrank a role before it can manage that role's permissions. (Roles above it that have Administrator are fine — they bypass channel permissions entirely, so the bot never needs to manage them.)
Web.Audit.Profile.PostAndPing: posts here and pings a role
Web.Audit.Profile.PostPinAndPing: posts, pins and pings a role here
Web.Audit.Profile.Draft: reads drafts and adds the severity reactions
Web.Audit.RequiredPermsOk: {icon:Ok} Hoshi's role has everything your enabled features need at server level.
Web.Audit.RequiredPermsNote: These exist only server-wide — assigning roles to members, renaming them, and creating channels cannot be granted on a single channel. Features that need them simply don't work until the role has them, and there is nothing below to fix instead.
Web.Audit.OptionalPermsHeading: Optional — lets Hoshi fix channels itself
Web.Audit.OptionalPermsOk: {icon:Ok} Hoshi can repair channel permissions itself.
Web.Audit.OptionalPermsNote: Entirely your call. These can also be granted per channel, and a channel can grant Hoshi something its role doesn't have — so declining here costs nothing except convenience. Granting them means Hoshi works in any channel without setup, and the Fix buttons below can repair a channel on their own (they can never grant a permission Hoshi doesn't already hold).
Web.Audit.FeatureAccessIntro: What each enabled feature needs in the channels you pointed it at, and whether Hoshi has it.
Web.Audit.UnauditableNote: Not listed here because they have no fixed channel: {features}. Hoshi posts wherever it was addressed, so its access depends on that channel.
Web.Audit.BotLacksManageRoles: Bot lacks Manage Roles permission in this server.
Web.Audit.BotRoleOutranked: Bot's role ({botRole}) doesn't outrank {role} — move the bot's role higher.
Web.Audit.BotCannotGrant: Bot doesn't hold these permissions itself, so it can't grant them: {permissions}.
Web.Audit.BotNoRole: Bot has no assignable role to grant a channel override to.
Web.Audit.ChannelNotFound: Channel not found in this guild (deleted, or not visible to the bot).
Web.Audit.FixedViaCategory: {icon:Ok} Fixed via the category — the bot now has the access it needs here.
Web.Audit.FixedOnChannel: {icon:Ok} Fixed on the channel — the bot now has the access it needs here.
Web.Audit.CategoryUpdatedChannelMissing: Category updated, but the channel is still missing some of what it needs — use "Fix on channel".
Web.Audit.CategoryUpdatedNotSynced: {icon:Text.Warning} Category updated, but this channel doesn't inherit from it (its permissions aren't synced). A channel the bot can't see can't be fixed automatically — grant Hoshi Bot access to it manually in Discord.
Web.Audit.ChannelFixStillMissing: {icon:Text.Warning} Overwrite applied on the channel, but the bot still lacks the required access. Check that its role isn't out-ranked and that another overwrite doesn't deny the needed permissions.
Web.Audit.FixRefusedVisible: {icon:Text.Warning} Discord refused the change — the bot can see this {level} but isn't allowed to change its permissions here (it needs the Manage Permissions right on it). Grant Hoshi Bot access to this {level} manually in Discord.
Web.Audit.FixRefusedInvisible: {icon:Text.Warning} Discord refused the change (Missing Access) — the bot can't edit a {level} it can't see. Grant Hoshi Bot access to it manually in Discord.
Web.Audit.FixRejected: {icon:Text.Warning} Discord rejected the change ({status}). Check the bot's Manage Roles permission and role position.
Web.Audit.FixExpectationError: Could not update the permission overwrite on Discord — does the bot have Manage Roles/Manage Channels permission in this server?
Web.Audit.BotPostingAccessIntro: Every channel the bot is configured to post to (feature channels, alert channels, and the guild's Settings channels), checked for the permissions the bot actually needs there — View Channel, Send Messages, Embed Links (its messages are embeds), plus Read Message History where it reads messages back. A channel it can't post to is silently skipped at send time — this is where that shows up.
Web.Audit.NoPostToChannelsConfigured: No post-to channels are configured for this guild yet.
Web.Audit.CantFixCalloutTitle: Some channels can't be fixed from here — what to do
Web.Audit.CantFixCalloutIntro: When a row says Can't see channel and offers no working fix button, Discord is hiding that channel from the bot entirely. Discord won't let a bot change a channel it can't even see, so you have to grant access once by hand in Discord — after that, the fix buttons on this page take over. In Discord:
Web.Audit.CantFixStep1: Right-click the category the channel sits in (its name is on the blue “Fix on category” button) → Edit Category → Permissions.
Web.Audit.CantFixStep2: Click the ＋ next to “Roles/Members” and add the Hoshi Bot role.
Web.Audit.CantFixStep3: Turn on View Channel (and Send Messages if the bot should post there) — the green {icon:Text.Check}.
Web.Audit.CantFixStep4: If a channel still shows red afterwards, right-click that channel → Edit Channel → Permissions → Sync Now so it inherits the category, then hit Re-check here.
Web.Audit.CantFixCalloutOutro: Don't want to touch each category? Giving the Hoshi Bot role the Administrator permission also works and skips all of this — but it removes every channel restriction for the bot, so the steps above are the safer choice.
Web.Audit.CantFixAutomaticallyNote: This channel can't be fixed automatically from here — grant the Hoshi Bot role the permissions listed under Status to the channel itself in Discord (see the note above), then Re-check.

Web.Me.Lead: Your personal Hoshi settings. Only you can change what's here.
Web.Me.LinkOk: Discord account linked — both accounts now share your player accounts.
Web.Me.LinkSelf: That's the account you're already signed in as. Sign in as the other one on Discord's page.
Web.Me.LinkNoPlayers: Connect a player account first — a shared player is what links two Discord accounts.
Web.Me.LinkFailed: Linking didn't complete. Please try again.
Web.Me.PlayerAccountsLead: Your in-game commanders. Hoshi uses them to give you the right roles and nickname in each community — pick which one represents you where under My Communities below.
Web.Me.PlayerAlreadyLinked: {name} is already linked to another Discord account. If that's your account, link it under My Discord Accounts below and this player will show up here.
Web.Me.NoCommunities: No communities to show — either Hoshi isn't in any of your Discord servers yet, or Discord didn't answer just now. Try again in a moment.
Web.Me.ConnectPlayerToGetRoles: Connect a player account to get roles here.
Web.Me.LanguageLead: The language Hoshi uses when talking to you personally — private replies, DMs and your tickets. Public channel posts follow the community's language instead.
Web.Me.DiscordAccountsLead: Play from more than one Discord account? Link them and Hoshi treats them as one person — your player accounts, roles and lore follow you to all of them.
Web.Me.LinkAnotherAccountHint: You'll be sent to Discord — sign in there with the other account (use its "not you?" switcher) to prove it's yours. You stay signed in here either way.
Web.Me.ProfileLead: Here you can see and edit what Hoshi knows about you, so she addresses you the right way and can chat with you like a real community member. Only you can change your own entries.
Web.Me.NoCards: There's nothing for you to edit here right now (no matching community found).
Web.Me.BackgroundLabel: About you (whatever you'd like to share)
Web.Me.NicknameSuffixLead: An optional alias appended to your nickname in communities that sync it: [TAG] Player (Suffix). It's left off when the nickname would get too long for Discord, and each community can choose not to use it.
Web.Me.PeerLoreHeading: What others have said about you
Web.Me.PeerLoreLead: Notes contributed by other members. You can't edit them, but you can hide them — then Hoshi won't use them and the team takes another look.
